clue.text: "When I want to read a novel, I write one" ()

definitions.text: "When I want to read a novel, I write one" ()

parts.words: "When I want to read a novel, I write one" ()
parts.note: the clue gives a famous remark with its speaker left blank: the solver supplies the Victorian statesman-novelist who said it

explanation.walkthrough: The empty brackets are where the attribution would go; the answer is the person quoted, the Tory premier who wrote fiction alongside his political career.
explanation.definitionFit: The quip is attributed to the Conservative prime minister who also wrote novels such as Sybil and Coningsby.

clue.text: "Whose souls, seduced by his erring eyes / Doth some proud Dame devoutly" (Joshua Sylvester)

definitions.text: "Whose souls, seduced by his erring eyes / Doth some proud Dame devoutly" (Joshua Sylvester)

parts.words: "Whose souls, seduced by his erring eyes / Doth some proud Dame devoutly" (Joshua Sylvester)
parts.note: a couplet from the Elizabethan translator stops short of its final verb, which the solver must restore: something done devoutly to a proud lady

explanation.walkthrough: This is a completion clue: the quotation lacks its last word, and the answer fills the gap, spelt with the -ize ending the grid uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to worship or adore excessively, which fits a soul devoutly adoring a proud dame.

clue.text: Hope-inspired romantic setting

parts.note: Hope looks like the feeling of optimism, but it is the novelist Anthony Hope, who invented an imaginary kingdom for The Prisoner of Zenda

explanation.surface: An optimistic, romantic backdrop for a love story.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope set his swashbuckling romances in this invented Central European kingdom.

clue.text: Curious sex lie circulated by Joyce

indicators.note: curious means odd or strange, so the following letters are to be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A strange sexual falsehood spread about by someone called Joyce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges SEXLIE; Joyce is James Joyce, whose only play has this title.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce published a play under this title in 1918, so it is a work he put into circulation.

clue.text: Bizet's creation a version of novel

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworked form of it, so the composer's name and the words before are rearranged

parts.note: the composer's name with its S counts as fodder here

explanation.surface: A new adaptation of the composer's opera, such as a reworking of Carmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges BIZETS plus CREATION plus A into the Alistair MacLean thriller title.
explanation.definitionFit: Alistair MacLean wrote a 1963 thriller of this name, about a polar research base, later filmed.

clue.text: Provenance of Alexander's boy, pace Mary Renault

definitions.text: Provenance of Alexander's boy, pace Mary Renault

parts.words: Provenance of Alexander's boy, pace Mary Renault
parts.note: Mary Renault's novel The ... Boy is about Bagoas, a young eunuch favoured by Alexander the Great; the clue asks where that boy came from

explanation.surface: Asking where Alexander the Great's favourite youth came from, with a nod to a historical novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pace' means 'with due respect to': the country is named by the title of Renault's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagoas, the narrator of Renault's novel, came from the ancient empire Alexander conquered, roughly modern Iran.

clue.text: Quiet boy, associated with gradualism, on the French prince in Shakespeare

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
Eric, or Little by Little is F. W. Farrar's Victorian school story, so this boy goes step by step
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken lad who takes things slowly sits on top of a French royal in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little by Little' is gradualism, the subtitle of Farrar's novel Eric; 'on' just puts the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Tyre is the title character of a late Shakespeare romance.

clue.text: Moore's man from Missouri?

parts.note: Missouri is the Show-Me State, so its man refuses to believe without proof; Thomas Moore wrote a satirical poem with this doubter's title

explanation.surface: Asking who Moore's character from Missouri might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter who demands evidence is the kind of person Missouri's 'show me' motto describes.

clue.text: Governess from Acton

parts.note: Acton looks like the London district, but Acton Bell was Anne Brontë's pen name, and her first novel's heroine is a governess

explanation.surface: A nanny who comes from a suburb of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë, writing as Acton Bell, made a governess the title heroine of her 1847 novel.

clue.text: Fates show one artist in French person

indicators.note: in places the one-plus-artist pair inside the French word for me

parts.note: moi is French for me, the first person
I is the Roman numeral one
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Destiny is displayed by a single painter inside a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French person' is grammatical: the first-person pronoun moi, split as MO...I around IRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moirai are the Greek name for the three goddesses of destiny.

clue.text: Community member featured by James

definitions.meaning: a citizen of the ... Community, the old name for the EU
Henry James wrote a novel titled with the plural of this word

explanation.definitionFit: A national of an EU country is one of these, and Henry James's 1878 novel is The Europeans.

clue.text: "Can life beneath the sun / More littled be?" (Hardy)

definitions.text: "Can life beneath the sun / More littled be?" (Hardy)

parts.words: "Can life beneath the sun / More littled be?" (Hardy)
parts.note: lines from Thomas Hardy asking whether life could be made any smaller; the answer is the superlative of little

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: Hardy's coinage 'littled' points to the superlative of little.
explanation.definitionFit: Being made smaller than anything else is the superlative degree of small.

clue.text: Silent stout adventurer from parliament

definitions.meaning: Keats's sonnet has stout Cortez staring at the Pacific, silent, upon a peak in Darien
the Spanish parliament is called the ...

explanation.surface: A quiet, burly explorer who emerges from a legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats names the conquistador in his sonnet on Chapman's Homer, and the same word is Spain's legislature.

clue.text: They had a dream in Edgar's piece

definitions.text: They had a dream in Edgar's piece

parts.words: They had a dream in Edgar's piece
parts.note: David Edgar's 1979 play Teendreams, written with Susan Todd, is about young people's dreams

explanation.surface: Someone had a dream in a work by somebody called Edgar.
explanation.definitionFit: David Edgar and Susan Todd's play Teendreams is about adolescents, people aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Male ferret attacked small humanoid

annotationWithheld.why: Male ferret attacked small humanoid (3,6): HE + HOB + BIT gives only HEHOBBIT; the T of THE has no source in the clue as held (perhaps 'The male ferret' was printed)

clue.text: Public transport in Tennessee

definitions.meaning: Tennessee Williams wrote A ... Named Desire

explanation.surface: Getting about by bus or tram in a southern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram running on city tracks is a public vehicle, and one is named in Tennessee Williams's title.

clue.text: Pomfret's preference

parts.note: John Pomfret's 1700 poem describes the life he would pick, and its title names that preference

explanation.definitionFit: A preference is a selection, and Pomfret's best-known poem bears that title.

clue.text: Moral tales an afterthought about fit land

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the afterthought goes round the farmland word

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter
arable land is fit for ploughing and crops

explanation.surface: Improving stories added as an afterthought about good farming country.
explanation.definitionFit: Short stories that teach a moral lesson, like those told in the Gospels.

clue.text: Way to the top, a la 12, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged some other way, an anagram signal

parts.note: 12 refers to the answer of clue 12 across, the Spanish parliament

explanation.surface: A route to the summit, in the style of a conquistador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ALA plus CORTES, the 12-across answer, into a moving staircase.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase carries people up to a higher floor.

clue.text: Home of well-known fiddle offers new romance

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of the following word are reshaped

explanation.surface: The birthplace of a famous violin promises a fresh love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lombardy town was home to Stradivari and Amati, makers of famous violins.

clue.text: Beastly French artist?

parts.note: fauve is French for wild beast, the jibe that named the Matisse-led school of painters

explanation.surface: A nasty painter from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics called Matisse and Derain les fauves, wild beasts, so a member of that movement is beastly in name.

clue.text: Synopsis, namely, he put over on master

parts.note: sc, scilicet, means namely
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Someone sums things up and puts one over on his teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline or summary plan of something is a synopsis.

clue.text: Poetry with sex appeal in the Ukraine

parts.note: odes are poems

explanation.surface: Sexy verse written in eastern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea port is a city located in Ukraine.

clue.text: Jupiter holds church to account for tax collector

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the god's name goes round the other pieces

parts.note: Zeus is the Greek counterpart of Jupiter

indicators.note: to means joined on to, so church comes after account

parts.note: a/c, AC, is short for account

explanation.surface: The king of the gods makes the church answer for its dealings with a taxman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Luke's Gospel, the chief publican of Jericho climbed a sycamore to see Jesus.

clue.text: Drones, perhaps, or group of readers

definitions.meaning: the Drones is the gentlemen's club in P. G. Wodehouse's books, a club found in a book
a society that meets to discuss books

explanation.surface: Idle bees or a reading circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wodehouse's Drones is a club existing only in books, and a reading circle bears the same name.

clue.text: In England, singer Sandra Belloni provides note in Lamb

indicators.note: in places the musical note inside the essayist's pen name

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the name Elia
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer in England puts a note into a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: George Meredith's novel Emilia in England, later retitled Sandra Belloni, follows a young singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Meredith's heroine, the singer Sandra Belloni, is the title character of his novel set in England.

clue.text: Native American trail of Louise Erdrich

definitions.text: Native American trail of Louise Erdrich

parts.words: Native American trail of Louise Erdrich
parts.note: Louise Erdrich, an Ojibwe novelist, wrote a 1988 novel whose title also means footprints left behind

explanation.surface: A path followed by indigenous people, belonging to an American author.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a set of footprints, and that word is the title of Erdrich's novel about Ojibwe life.

clue.text: Can a late rewrite reveal bits and pieces of literature?

indicators.note: a rewrite produces a new arrangement of what was written, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a late revision could expose fragments of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of selected literary passages or extracts is called this.
